business_problem: Spirit AI needed high-efficiency compute infrastructure to train embodied AI models for long-horizon, flexible-object manipulation, because generic cloud training environments would waste costly compute time and slow down iteration on robotics foundation models.
solution_summary: Spirit AI used Baidu AI Cloud's high-performance AI infrastructure to train its Spirit v1 VLA model for embodied robotics. The project centers on the gap between research ambition and practical compute efficiency: Spirit needs to handle dynamic scene perception, long action sequences, and multimodal training while keeping cluster time productive enough to support rapid iteration. Baidu provided an AI infra platform and the BaiGe heterogeneous compute environment so Spirit could train vision-language-action models with more reliable scheduling and lower wasted time. Supporting acceleration tooling boosts both training and inference throughput, while the platform is being tuned for long-sequence and multimodal workloads that are specific to embodied-model development. This gives Spirit a compute-and-tooling foundation that can support future commercialization in manufacturing and services, where robots must learn complex language-conditioned actions instead of following narrow pre-programmed routines.

solution_components.role: Provides the stable cluster environment required to train embodied VLA models efficiently.

solution_components.name: Training and Inference Acceleration Suite
solution_components.role: Improves training throughput and inference performance so model iteration becomes faster and more cost-effective.

data_flow: Embodied-robotics datasets and task prompts are processed in the AI infra environment, where Spirit trains VLA models across heterogeneous compute resources. The acceleration suite improves the training and inference loop, and resulting model checkpoints are used to support downstream deployment for manufacturing and service robotics scenarios.
business_outcome: Spirit AI gained a more efficient training base for embodied models, reducing wasted compute and speeding iteration on robotics intelligence that it plans to commercialize in real-world tasks.
metrics: The acceleration suite improved training efficiency 30%.
